newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Five Vietnam banks sign cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Five Vietnam banks sign cooperation pact.

text.p: Five Ho Chi Minh City banks have set up a mutual fund to provide each other with cheap loans and have left the door open for other banks to join, the Saigon Times Daily said on Monday.
Officials at the five private banks -- Mekong, Dai Nam, Nam Do, Que Do and VP Bank -- were not immediately available to comment on the report.

The newspaper said the fund's capital was $29.7 million and quoted VP Bank's new director general, Huynh Buu Son, as saying that the banks had combined assets of over two trillion dong ($171.60 million) and 24 branches and transaction offices.
"The five banks last Thursday signed an agreement which particularly focuses on commitments to co-assistance, co-guarantee, cooperation in money remittance operations across the country..." it said.
It added that members of the association could receive loans from each other at preferential rates.
Son told Reuters last week that the association, then under discussion, would act as a clearing house for banks to settle their debts.
The plan has come at a time of growing concern about a liquidity crunch at many of the country's 53 privately held banks, which are known as joint-stock banks.

The problem came under the spotlight in February after it emerged that VP Bank, the first bank in Vietnam to take foreign shareholders, had failed to meet the payment deadline on a $3 million deferred letter of credit.

However, the Saigon Times Daily said the aim of the scheme was to meet hefty demand from bank clients for loans and get around regulations limiting banks to lending no more than the equivalent of 10 percent of their capital.
It said the "aligned bank" was an open organisation which other banks could join if existing member banks agreed.
